# Ed Martin launches new show to ‘name and shame’ Biden’s lawfare leaders

![Ed Martin speaks at an event at the Capitol in Washington, June 13, 2023. (AP Photo/Amanda Andrade-Rhoades, File)](https://twt-thumbs.washtimes.com/media/image/2026/08/21/Election_2_26_Ed_Martin_87771_c0-190-4492-2809_s885x516.jpg?2fbce35a0b6dfa58256a65f274e76337d9be05c5)
![Google](https://www.washingtontimes.com/static/icons/google/g.webp)

[![](https://media.washtimes.com/media/image/2026/01/15/SeenHeardWhispered-2550x375.jpg)](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/seen-heard-and-whispered/)

![](https://media.washtimes.com/media/image/2026/01/15/SeenHeardWhispered-2550x375.jpg)

[Ed Martin](/topics/ed-martin/), President Trump’s former pardon attorney and, briefly, his U.S. attorney in Washington, is starting a show on Monday to call out the people in the Biden administration who he believes weaponized the Justice Department against their opponents.

“The Early Bird” will air at 5 a.m. on weekdays on the Real America’s Voice TV channel and the Rumble video platform.

People were interested in these podcasts

His first show will feature an interview with a defendant from the [Jan. 6, 2021](/topics/jan-6-2021/), incursion at the Capitol.

Mr. Martin is also expected to share war stories from his time at the Justice Department, where he was interim U.S. attorney for Washington, then the pardon attorney.

He’ll also identify people he sees as part of a deep state resistance to Mr. Trump.

“He is going to name and shame them,” Mr. Martin’s spokesperson told “Seen, Heard & Whispered.”

The name of the program is taken from the daily internal Defense Department newsletter that compiled the previous day’s media stories for consumption by the administration’s movers and shakers each morning. It was discontinued in 2013.
